newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ long bond yields close 14 points higher.
newsitem.headline: NZ long bond yields close 14 points higher.

* NZ yields close higher on profit taking, dollar weakness
* Weaker currency undermines yields
* Eyes on jobs data due on Friday morning
New Zealand bond yields rose up to 14 points on Thursday as profit takers sold and currency concerns rose.
Dealers said selling was most pronounced in the long end of the market where the 10 year bonds rose 14 points against a five point move in the 90-day bills.
A sharply weaker Trade-Weighted Index, caused by the weakening of the U.S. dollar against the yen, underscored weakness already apparent, dealers said.
"That trend looks a bit negative at the moment and kiwi-yen looks pretty sick so you would have to argue the balance of risks suggests there is more downside there," a dealer said.
Direction in the bank bill market will be dictated by Friday morning's jobs data. Economists are picking quarterly employment growth of 0.2 percent and a participation rate of 65.8 percent.
"That will be crucial for the market for the next 10-15 points," said one dealer.
Bond dealers said the Australian market was "peeling off" and that gave local selling further impetus.
They said there was a chance U.S. Treasuries would weaken following the sharp fall in the dollar.
One said there was talk of Japan raising its official rates.

"If this dollar-yen starts to peel off then global markets could be a little bit concerned. That's one of the risks that's been around for a while. Maybe it's the start of a turnaround in monetary conditions in Japan."

He said there was the possibility of a sharp rate rise in Japan and that would have severe repercussions. Japanese inflows had been fuelling much of the debt market rallies in the dollar bloc and a reversal of flows could stymie those rallies.
